artifacts.role: executable continuation decision + atomic create-if-absent claim canary
race, sibling parallelism, authority, readiness and preserve-first verification

verification.method: git hash-object on the exact locally executed files equals the GitHub blob SHA returned after persistence for both script and test
cases: same-context + same-authority checkpoints remain in one run
context or authority change forces split/boundary
dependency-derived readiness requires proof refs and no failed/conflicted prerequisites
existing live claim/context change/authority escalation prevents successor claim
claim payload remains candidate-scoped and does not self-promote Current/Human Accepted/Served
two concurrent workers racing one exclusive successor yield exactly one winner/start permission
independent sibling successors use distinct claim paths and both remain parallel
preserve-first claim mutates only the append-only claim path and leaves opportunity inputs unchanged

atomicity_model.winner: only the worker whose exclusive create succeeds receives may_start_run=true
atomicity_model.sibling_parallelism: independent successors have distinct exclusive paths; no global continuation lock is introduced
atomicity_model.production_boundary: This canary proves the continuation state machine and atomic create-if-absent semantics in the executable candidate. Production GitHub/remote claim transport must preserve the same exclusive-create contract; no claim here promotes /w or global authority.

remaining_boundary: Integration with the live role-fluid allocator/dynamic-readiness implementation is a separate owner/integration step. This worker intentionally did not edit those concurrently owned files.
